proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly compares Khowar paránu, Palula purōṇo, Kohistani Shina pōṇṷ, Punjabi purānā, Assamese purān and Oriya puruṇā under purāṇa ancient/old. These whole survey adjectives fit that regional series, including shortened Kohistani por-/pur- forms and eastern purun-/purn- forms. The family comparison does not claim a detailed derivation of every nasal vowel or consonant reduction; extended or additional-word responses are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The adjective branch of cukra sour includes Bengali cuk/cukā acid, Assamese suksukiyā slightly acid and several northwestern cuk-/cūk- forms. Hajong cuku/cuka/cukau preserves this affricate-plus-velar sour stem with final-vowel variation. The adjective branch is used, rather than the separately defined drink or plant senses; the evidence establishes the regional family, not an independently demonstrated route for each ending.

proposals.evidence: Turner lists Assamese bā̃h and Bengali bā̃s bamboo together under vaṃśa, distinguishing the later vaṃśaka formation. Hajong bas and Bishnupriya baha agree with these eastern s/h bamboo forms. The survey lacks a nasalization mark, which is preserved rather than silently repaired; the s/h contrast alone is not used to assert borrowing from either modern language.
